skill.name: Skill Builder
skill.description: Create Claude Code skills with valid SKILL.md frontmatter, progressive disclosure structure, directory guidance, examples, and validation checklists.
skill.summary: Build structured Claude Code skills with templates, examples, and validation guidance.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown examples, fenced code, documentation links, and placeholder paths. The confirmed risk is direct creation and writing of files under ~/.claude/skills, which can persist new agent instructions. No prompt injection or data exfiltration language was found.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before creating or writing ~/.claude/skills, and show the exact paths before execution.
Prefer project-local .claude/skills for reviewed team workflows, or add a review step before installing personal skills.

remediation.issue: Placeholder commands and links in templates
remediation.suggestion: Label placeholder commands and URLs clearly, and tell users to adapt them before running or publishing.

static_findings.snippet: **Critical**: Only `name` and `description` are used by Claude. Additional fields are ignored.

finding_verdicts.reason: The quick-start bash block instructs running shell commands that create and write a skill under ~/.claude/skills. This is intended, but it changes persistent Claude configuration and needs user consent.

content.value_statement: Creating valid Claude or Codex skills can be hard when structure, metadata, and disclosure rules are unclear. This skill provides templates, checklists, and examples for building organized skills.
actual_capabilities: Explains required SKILL.md YAML frontmatter fields.
Shows personal and project skill directory layouts.
Provides minimal, intermediate, and advanced skill templates.
Documents progressive disclosure levels and file navigation patterns.
Includes a validation checklist for skill structure and content.
Links to Claude skill documentation and examples.
limitations: Does not include executable helper scripts.
Does not validate generated skills automatically.
Examples use placeholder commands and URLs that require adaptation.
Focuses on Claude Code skill structure, not every marketplace rule.

use_cases.title: Create a Personal Workflow Skill
use_cases.description: Build a clear skill for repeated local development, writing, or research tasks.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Skill Structure
use_cases.description: Define shared project skills with consistent metadata, folders, resources, and review checklists.

use_cases.title: Prepare Marketplace Skill Content
use_cases.description: Draft skill instructions, examples, and validation steps before packaging a public skill.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal skill for [workflow]. Include the required name and description fields. Add a short quick start and checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Add File Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a project skill for [team workflow]. Show the SKILL.md outline, folder layout, and resource files that should exist.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Existing Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current skill instructions for [goal]. Suggest frontmatter, disclosure levels, examples, and file references that improve usability.

prompt_templates.title: Build Full Skill Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a full skill plan for [domain]. Include templates, scripts, resources, tests, and publishing checks for Claude Code and Codex users.

output_examples.input: I need a skill that helps write release notes for product teams.
output_examples.output: A structured release-notes skill outline with frontmatter guidance, quick start steps, resource suggestions, and a validation checklist.

output_examples.input: Improve this skill so Claude loads less context.
output_examples.output: A progressive disclosure rewrite that keeps core instructions in SKILL.md and moves long references into docs and resources.

output_examples.input: Plan an advanced skill with scripts and templates.
output_examples.output: A package plan covering script purpose, resource folders, usage steps, and testing notes without generating executable files directly.

best_practices: Keep SKILL.md concise and move long references into separate files.
Write descriptions that explain both what the skill does and when to use it.
Review generated commands and paths before running or publishing a skill.
anti_patterns: Do not bury trigger words in long descriptions.
Do not place skills inside unsupported nested namespaces.
Do not publish placeholder commands, URLs, or scripts without review.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It helps create Claude Code skill instructions, folder plans, templates, and validation checklists.

faq.question: Does it generate executable scripts?
faq.answer: No. It documents where scripts can live and shows examples that need review before use.

faq.question: Can I use it for team skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains project-local skill placement and version-controlled team workflows.

faq.question: Does it support Codex users?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata declares Codex support, and prompts can target Codex workflows.

faq.question: What should I review before publishing?
faq.answer: Review frontmatter, directory placement, examples, resource links, script references, and security-sensitive paths.

faq.question: Is it safe to run every example directly?
faq.answer: No. Treat commands as templates and confirm paths, dependencies, and effects before running them.
